questions.text: The dual of a Boolean function [latex]F(x_{1},x_{2},...,x_{n}, +, \cdot , ' ) [/latex] , written as [latex]F^{D}[/latex], is the same expression as that of F with + and  [latex]\cdot[/latex]  swapped. F is said to be self-dual if [latex]F=F^{D}[/latex].  The number of self-dual functions with n Boolean variables is
questions.solution:
A self-dual function satisfies [latex]F(\bar x_1,\dots,\bar x_n)=\overline{F(x_1,\dots,x_n)}[/latex].

The [latex]2^n[/latex] input rows form [latex]2^{n-1}[/latex] complementary pairs. Choosing F on one row of a pair fixes F on the other, so we freely choose [latex]2^{n-1}[/latex] bits.

Number of self-dual functions = [latex]2^{2^{n-1}}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]2^{2^{n-1}}[/latex]

questions.text:
Consider the 4-to-1 multiplexer with two lines S1 and S0 given below.

The minimal sum of-products form of the Boolean expression for the output F of the multiplexer is
questions.solution:
Selects S1 = P, S0 = Q:
[latex]F=\bar P\bar Q\cdot0+\bar PQ\cdot1+P\bar Q\cdot R+PQ\cdot\bar R[/latex]
[latex]\bar PQ+PQ\bar R=Q(\bar P+\bar R)=\bar PQ+Q\bar R[/latex]

[latex]F=\bar PQ+Q\bar R+P\bar QR[/latex]

Answer: Option 1

questions.text:
The base (or radix) of the number system such that the following equation holds is_______.
[latex]\frac{312}{20}=13.1[/latex]
questions.solution:
In base b: [latex]312=3b^2+b+2[/latex], [latex]20=2b[/latex], [latex]13.1=b+3+\frac1b[/latex].
[latex]3b^2+b+2=2b\left(b+3+\frac1b\right)=2b^2+6b+2\Rightarrow b^2=5b\Rightarrow b=5[/latex]

Answer: 5

questions.text:
Consider the following Boolean Algebra for F:
[latex]F(P,Q,R,S)=PQ+\bar{P}QR+\bar{P}Q\bar{R}S[/latex]
The minimal sum-of products form of F is
questions.solution:
[latex]F=Q(P+\bar PR+\bar P\bar RS)=Q(P+R+S)=PQ+QR+QS[/latex] (using [latex]P+\bar PR=P+R[/latex] and [latex]R+\bar RS=R+S[/latex]).

Answer: PQ+QR+QS
